name: Banana oat muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
In a large bowl, whisk the wheat flour, the rolled oats, the baking powder and the cinnamon.
In another bowl, mix the mashed banana, the egg, the cow's milk and the canola oil until smooth.
Pour the wet mixture over the dry and fold with a spatula just until no dry flour shows. Lumps are fine.
Divide between the 12 cups; they should be about three-quarters full.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the centre comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes in the tin, then on a rack. Under 12 months, break into pea-sized pieces. Freezes up to 2 months.

name: Fluffy pancakes
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the wheat flour with the baking powder.
In a jug, beat the eggs with the cow's milk.
Pour the milk mixture over the flour and whisk just until smooth; a few small lumps are fine. Rest 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and brush it with a little of the canola oil, about 30 seconds, until it shimmers.
Pour 60 ml of batter per pancake. Cook 2 minutes, until bubbles form on top and the edges look set.
Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until golden underneath. Oil the pan again between batches.
Cut into strips for a baby, quarters for a toddler. Freeze between sheets of parchment, up to 1 month.

name: Lentil and carrot patties
steps: Drain the cooked lentils well and mash them roughly with a fork in a large bowl; leave some texture.
Grate the cooked carrot and mince the garlic. Add both to the lentils.
Add the egg, the breadcrumbs and the salt. Mix with a spoon until it holds together when pressed.
Shape into 10 patties about 6 cm across and 1 cm thick. Chill 10 minutes so they firm up.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and crisp at the edges. Do not crowd the pan.
Drain on paper towel. Under 12 months, break a patty into pea-sized pieces. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Sweet potato and chicken purée
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Cut the chicken into 1 cm pieces, trimming any fat.
Warm the olive oil in a small pot over medium heat, about 30 seconds, until it shimmers.
Add the chicken and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Add the sweet potato and the chicken broth. Cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the sweet potato mashes easily with a fork.
Blend smooth for 6 months, or mash with a fork from 9 months. Loosen with a spoon of broth if too thick.
Cool to lukewarm before serving. Keeps 2 days in the fridge, or freeze in an ice-cube tray.

name: Apple cinnamon oatmeal
steps: Peel, core and grate the apple on the large holes of a box grater.
Pour the cow's milk into a small pot with the rolled oats and the cinnamon. Stir once.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, about 3 minutes, stirring, until small bubbles break the surface.
Add the grated apple and cook 5 to 6 minutes more, stirring often, until the oats are soft and the oatmeal is thick.
Take off the heat and let it stand 2 minutes; it thickens as it cools.
Serve lukewarm. Under 12 months, blend or thin with a spoon of milk. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

name: Date energy bites
steps: Check the pitted dates for stones and chop them roughly.
Put the dates, the natural peanut butter and the vanilla extract in a food processor. Pulse 30 seconds, until it forms a sticky paste.
Add the rolled oats and the chia seeds. Pulse 20 seconds more, until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Wet your hands and roll into 15 balls the size of a walnut.
Chill 30 minutes on a plate, until firm.
Store in a sealed container: 1 week in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Not for under 12 months; halve for toddlers.

name: Pasta in rosé sauce with chicken
steps: Dice the onion, mince the garlic and cut the chicken into 1 cm pieces.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, about 8 minutes, until it bubbles hard.
Cook the wheat pasta in the boiling water 1 minute less than the package says, until just tender. Drain, keeping 125 ml of the water.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and the salt. Simmer 8 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in the heavy cream and the drained pasta; add pasta water a spoon at a time until the sauce coats every piece.
Cool to lukewarm. Under 12 months, chop the pasta and chicken small. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Baked fish nuggets
steps: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment and brush it with half the canola oil.
Pat the white fish dry with paper towel and cut it into 12 fingers about 2 cm wide. Check for bones with your fingertips.
Grate the onion finely into a shallow bowl, add the egg and the salt, and beat with a fork.
Spread the breadcrumbs on a plate.
Dip each finger in the egg, let it drip, then roll it in the breadcrumbs, pressing so they stick. Set on the sheet.
Drizzle the remaining canola oil over the nuggets.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden and the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Cool 5 minutes. Under 12 months, flake a nugget into small pieces; toddlers eat them whole. Best the same day.

name: Silky hummus
steps: Drain and rinse the cooked chickpeas.
Peel the garlic. Blend the tahini, the lemon juice and the garlic 30 seconds, until pale and creamy.
Add the chickpeas and half the water. Run 1 minute, scraping down the sides once.
With the motor running, pour in the olive oil and the remaining water. Blend 1 minute more, until smooth and silky.
Taste; add a spoon of water if it is thicker than you like.
Spread thin on toast fingers under 12 months, or serve with soft cooked vegetable sticks. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

name: Banana bread
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease a 23 × 13 cm loaf pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Melt the butter in a small pot over low heat, about 2 minutes, until liquid, then let it cool a little.
In a large bowl, whisk the mashed banana, the eggs, the sugar, the melted butter and the vanilla extract until smooth.
In another bowl, whisk the wheat flour, the baking powder and the baking soda.
Fold the dry mixture into the banana mixture with a spatula, just until no dry flour shows. Lumps are fine.
Pour into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, until deep golden and a toothpick in the centre comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then on a rack. Under 12 months, cut a slice into fingers. Keeps 3 days; freezes 2 months.

name: Oatmeal raisin cookies
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Soak the raisins in hot water 5 minutes, until plump, then drain and chop them roughly.
In a large bowl, beat the softened butter with the sugar 1 minute, until pale and creamy. Beat in the egg.
In another bowl, whisk the wheat flour, the rolled oats, the cinnamon and the baking soda.
Add the dry mixture to the butter mixture with the raisins. Stir just until no dry flour shows.
Drop tablespoons of dough onto the sheet, 5 cm apart, and flatten each one slightly with wet fingers.
Bake 11 to 13 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centres still look soft.
Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack. Not for under 12 months; halve for toddlers. Keeps 4 days in a tin.

name: Mini vegetable frittatas
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Brush 8 cups of a muffin tin with the olive oil.
Grate the zucchini and squeeze it dry in a clean towel. Chop the spinach finely.
In a bowl, beat the eggs with the cow's milk until no streaks of white remain.
Stir in the zucchini, the spinach and the grated cheddar.
Divide between the 8 cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until puffed, set in the centre and lightly golden at the edges.
Cool 5 minutes, then run a knife around each one. Under 12 months, cut into strips. Keeps 3 days; freezes 1 month.

name: Squash and coconut soup
steps: Peel the butternut squash, scoop out the seeds and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Dice the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the onion and cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the squash and the chicken broth. Cover and simmer 15 to 18 minutes, until the squash crushes easily against the pot.
Pour in the coconut milk and heat 2 minutes, until steaming, without boiling.
Blend smooth with an immersion blender, about 1 minute, until velvety.
Cool to lukewarm. From 12 months, add a few cooked pasta shapes. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freezes 2 months.

name: Mac and cheese with hidden squash
steps: Peel the butternut squash and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Steam 10 to 12 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, about 8 minutes, until it bubbles hard.
Cook the wheat pasta 1 minute less than the package says, until just tender. Drain.
Mash the steamed squash smooth with a fork, or blend it with a splash of the cow's milk.
Melt the butter in the empty pot over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it foams. Whisk in the wheat flour for 1 minute.
Pour in the cow's milk a little at a time, whisking. Cook 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in the grated cheddar, the mashed squash and the salt, about 1 minute, until the cheese melts.
Fold in the pasta. Under 12 months, chop the pasta small. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Turkey and apple meatballs
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and grate the apple on the large holes of a box grater, then squeeze out the juice with your hands.
Mince the garlic. In a large bowl, beat the egg with the Dijon mustard and the salt.
Add the ground turkey, grated apple, garlic and breadcrumbs. Mix with your fingertips just until combined.
Wet your hands and roll into 20 balls the size of a ping-pong ball. Space them out on the sheet.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until browned on top and no pink remains in the centre (74 °C inside).
Rest 3 minutes. Under 12 months, mash one with a fork; for toddlers, quarter them. Freezes cooked, up to 2 months.

name: Vanilla rice pudding
steps: Cook the rice in the milk over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often.
Add the maple syrup and vanilla at the end of cooking.
Serve warm, dusted with cinnamon.

name: Mango banana smoothie
steps: Blend all the ingredients until smooth.
Serve with a spoon or in a sippy cup, depending on age.

name: Chewy granola bars
steps: Gently warm the peanut butter, honey and oil.
Pour over the oats, raisins and nuts, then mix well.
Press firmly into a parchment-lined pan.
Bake at 160 °C for 20 minutes, then cool completely before cutting.

name: Vanilla chia pudding
steps: Whisk the chia, milk, syrup and vanilla.
Refrigerate for 4 hours, whisking once after 30 minutes.
Top with blueberries just before serving.

name: Yogurt dip with vegetable sticks
steps: Squeeze the grated cucumber dry in a clean cloth.
Stir into the yogurt with the lemon and garlic.
Serve with vegetables prepared to suit the child's age.

name: Salmon and sweet potato cakes
steps: Peel the sweet potato, cut it into 2 cm cubes and steam 12 minutes, until a fork slides in easily. Mash it in a large bowl.
Check the salmon for bones with your fingertips, then chop it finely with a knife until it looks like coarse mince.
Slice the green onion thinly and chop the dill. Zest the lemon half.
Add the salmon, green onion, dill and lemon zest to the sweet potato. Mix with a spoon until it holds together when pressed.
Shape into 10 flat cakes about 6 cm across. Chill 10 minutes, until firm.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Cook the cakes 4 minutes per side, until golden and the salmon inside is opaque all the way through.
Under 12 months, break a cake into small flakes; toddlers eat them whole. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; freezes 1 month.

name: White bean and tomato stew
steps: Dice the onion and the carrot small. Mince the garlic. Drain and rinse the white beans.
Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the onion and carrot and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and the dried oregano and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and the vegetable broth. Simmer 10 minutes, until the carrot is tender.
Add the beans and simmer 5 minutes more, until heated through and the stew thickens slightly.
Mash a ladle of beans against the pot to thicken it. Under 12 months, blend a portion smooth. Keeps 4 days; freezes 2 months.

name: Chicken and broccoli rice
steps: Rinse the brown rice in a sieve until the water runs clear. Cut the chicken into 1 cm pieces and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the chicken and cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Add the garlic and the rice and stir 1 minute, until the grains look glossy.
Pour in the chicken broth. Cover and simmer 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the broth is absorbed.
Cut the broccoli into small florets. Lay them on top of the rice, cover, and steam 5 minutes, until bright green and tender.
Stir everything together. Under 12 months, chop the broccoli and chicken small and moisten with a spoon of water. Keeps 3 days.

name: Lentil shepherd's pie
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and boil 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Dice the onion and the carrot small. Drain the cooked lentils.
Heat half the olive oil in a pan over medium heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers. Cook the onion and carrot 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute, until it darkens. Add the lentils, the green peas and the vegetable broth.
Simmer 8 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Spread in a 20 × 20 cm baking dish.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the remaining olive oil until smooth. Spread over the lentils and rough up the top with a fork.
Bake 20 minutes, until the top is golden at the ridges and the edges bubble.
Rest 10 minutes. Under 12 months, mash a portion with a fork. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freezes 2 months.

name: Tofu and vegetable fried rice
steps: Press the firm tofu between paper towels 10 minutes, then cut it into 1 cm cubes. Grate the carrot and slice the green onion.
Beat the eggs in a bowl. Use cooked rice that is cold from the fridge; it fries without turning gummy.
Heat half the canola oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Cook the tofu 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Set aside on a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the carrot and cook 2 minutes, until softened. Pour in the eggs and stir 1 minute, until just set.
Add the rice and the green peas and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes, until the rice is hot and slightly crisp at the edges.
Return the tofu, add the coconut aminos and the green onion, and toss 30 seconds, until coated.
Under 12 months, chop the tofu smaller and skip the crisp edges. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
